sentences.text: Empire Exports & Anr vs Union Of India & Ors on 16 July, 2013

Author: Harish Tandon
Bench: Harish Tandon
 Wp No. 602 of 2013
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction
 Original Side
 Empire Exports & Anr.
 Versus
 Union of India & Ors.
Before:
The Hon'ble Justice Harish Tandon
Date: 16th July 2013
 Appearance:

Mr. Rajdeep Ray, Advocate
 Mr. Bhaskar Vaisya, Advocate
 Mr. Ratul Biswas, Advocate
 for the petitioner
 Mr. Ramdulal Manna, Advocate
 for Union of India
 Mr. R. Bharadwaj, Advocate
 Mrs. Kanta Ray, Advocate
 for customs authorities
 The Court:

The writ petition is taken out by the petitioner for an order directing the respondent-authorities to draw fresh samples from the imported boiled Chikeni Supari Peppermit flavoured 2013 for retesting and with further prayer to release the said consignment.
The petitioner tried to contend before this Court that the authorities have treated those goods as a raw material of pan masala coming under Regulation 2.3.47 and not fit for human consumption.
The aforesaid stand is taken by the customs authorities on the basis of a report of one S. K. Mitra Private Limited, a laboratory set up in Kolkata, which is annexed to this writ petition.
According to the petitioner, the goods imported are coming under the Regulation 2.11.5 and therefore, the stand of the customs authorities are not entertainable at all.

The respondent-authorities placed before me the order dated 21st May 2013 issued by the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India indicating the names of the referral food laboratory for the respective States and Union Territories.

sentences.text: The respondent now says that if the petitioner so intends,
retesting
can be made to the referral laboratory although there is no prayer in this regard.

This Court does not find that there is any embargo in making a prayer for retesting in a referral food laboratory if there is any doubt and suspicion in the report so relied upon by the authorities concerned.
The petitioner is much emphatic on the assertion that it should be done within the territory of Kolkata and not otherwise.

This Court finds that the said order was passed in exercise of powers conferred under Section 43(2) of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006 and therefore, this Court does not find any justification in the submission of the petitioner.

Since the authorities have agreed for the retesting this Court, therefore, directs the concerned authority to send the samples which have been tested in the S. K. Mitra Private Limited, a laboratory stationed in Kolkata, to be sent to the referral food laboratory in terms of the said order dated 21st May 2013.
The samples shall be sent by the concerned authority within a week from date.

The authority concerned shall see that the report from the concerned referral food laboratory is received within three weeks from the date of sending of the samples for retesting and after receiving the report a copy where of shall be supplied to the petitioner.
With these observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
There will be no order as to costs.
All parties are to act on a signed photocopy of this order on the usual undertakings.
(Harish Tandon, J.) R. Bose AR(CR)
